questions.question: What does physical geography study?
choices: Only election districts
Only language distribution
Natural features and processes of Earth
Only international trade prices

questions.question: What is weathering?
choices: Breakdown of rock at or near Earth's surface
Transport of sediment from one place to another
Accumulation of sediment in a new location
Movement of people into a city

questions.question: What is erosion?
choices: Breakdown of rock without transport
Removal and transport of rock or sediment
Cooling of molten rock underground
The creation of a political boundary

questions.question: What is deposition?
choices: The movement of plates without surface effects
The removal of all sediment from a region
The breakdown of rock in place only
The settling or accumulation of transported material

questions.question: What is a watershed?
choices: An area draining water to a common outlet
A boundary separating languages
An area receiving no precipitation
A national district used only for elections

questions.question: What is a delta?
choices: A steep cliff formed only by earthquakes
A mountain peak shaped only by wind
A sediment-built landform near a river's mouth
A dry basin with no river connection

questions.question: What is a plateau?
choices: A narrow sea inlet between steep cliffs
An elevated area with a relatively level surface
A low coastal marsh at sea level
A deep trench on the ocean floor

questions.question: How can moving tectonic plates shape landscapes?
choices: They change only the amount of rainfall
They determine every cultural boundary
They prevent earthquakes from occurring
They can build mountains, produce faults, and generate volcanic activity

questions.question: What happens at a convergent plate boundary?
choices: Plates move toward one another
Plates move apart
Plates slide past one another only
No relative movement occurs

questions.question: How can glaciers reshape land?
choices: Ice has no effect on rock beneath it
Glaciers operate only in tropical lowlands
Moving ice erodes rock and transports sediment
Glaciers form all rivers through volcanic activity

questions.question: Why do rivers often deposit sediment when flow slows?
choices: Slower water always carries larger particles than fast water
Slower water has less ability to carry some sediment
Sediment can settle only on mountain summits
Rivers transport only dissolved gases

questions.question: How does groundwater relate to surface water?
choices: The two systems are always completely disconnected
Groundwater exists only beneath oceans
All groundwater remains permanently frozen
Water can move between underground storage and streams or springs

questions.question: What processes connect stages of the water cycle?
choices: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and movement through land and water
Only volcanic eruptions and earthquakes
Only political changes and urban migration
Only tides and changes in currency values

questions.question: Why do floodplains often have fertile soils?
choices: Floodplains never receive sediment
Every floodplain consists only of bare rock
Flooding can deposit nutrient-bearing sediment
Flooding permanently prevents plant growth

questions.question: Why can landforms change at different rates?
choices: All landforms change at exactly the same speed
Slow processes and sudden events can both reshape terrain
Only human construction changes landscapes
Every mountain forms in a single storm

questions.question: A rock cracks as water repeatedly freezes in its openings. Which process is illustrated?
choices: River deposition
Ocean circulation
Population migration
Physical weathering

questions.question: A stream carries sand downstream and drops it where the current slows. Which sequence occurs?
choices: Erosion followed by deposition
Deposition followed by weathering only
Condensation followed by volcanic eruption
Mountain building followed by immigration

questions.question: A map traces streams flowing into one lake. What area can be identified?
choices: A language region
An electoral district
The lake's watershed
A trade currency zone

questions.question: Two plates move apart and new crust forms between them. Which boundary is involved?
choices: Convergent boundary
Divergent boundary
Transform boundary
A boundary without plate motion

questions.question: A coastal community studies elevation and nearby river channels before planning development. What physical-geography concern is central?
choices: The national election calendar
The legal ownership of foreign currencies
The historical spelling of the town's name
Exposure to flooding and related land-water conditions
